Gigabytes per second (log scale) · higher is better

g.title: Click to hide or show BLAKE3
portable compression: Fewer than four whole chunks: each runs through the portable single-chunk compressor, so 2 KiB and 3 KiB take this path too.
NEON hash_many (4-way): Four whole chunks fill a NEON batch; from here the bulk of the input runs four chunks at a time.
Click to hide or show SHA-256
sha2 aarch64_sha2 backend (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions): One kernel at every size.

g.text: SHA-256: sha2 0.11.0 · single-threaded · sha2 aarch64_sha2 backend (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions)

g.title: Click to hide or show SHA-1DC
SHA-1 with collision detection, pure Rust: One kernel at every size.
Click to hide or show BLAKE3 servil
scalar kernel c1, one call: Inputs of one chunk (1 KiB) or less run every block, the root compression included, in one call to the integer-only kernel, with the state in registers throughout.

integer + NEON hybrid kernels: Above one chunk the tree is hashed several chunks at a time; below a full SME2 group of sixteen, the hybrid kernels run scalar chunks on the integer units beside NEON chunks, up to fifteen per call.
SME2 hash16_chunks kernel: Sixteen whole chunks fill one group on 512-bit streaming vectors, up to eight groups per call; a remainder below sixteen stays on the hybrid kernels.

g.text: BLAKE3 servil: source https://github.com/johnservil/BLAKE3 · branch sme2-bench · commit 4f8118b6f084 · clean

g.title: Click to hide or show SHA-256 ring
sha256_block_data_order_hw (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions, pipelined schedule): One kernel at every size.

g.text: SHA-256 ring: ring 0.17.14 · single-threaded · sha256_block_data_order_hw (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions, pipelined schedule)

g.title: Click to hide or show BLAKE3 mt
caller's thread (below one SIMD width of chunks): One SIMD width of chunks or less is one hash_many call; update_rayon has nothing to split.
rayon::join over the pool: Above one SIMD width of chunks the tree splits recursively with rayon::join, and idle pool threads steal the halves.

g.text: BLAKE3 mt: blake3 1.8.7 · Hasher::update_rayon · platform NEON
BLAKE3 mt: Rayon's global pool, at its default size (one thread per logical CPU)

g.title: Click to hide or show BLAKE3 servil mt
scalar kernel c1, one call: Inputs of one chunk (1 KiB) or less run every block, the root compression included, in one call to the integer-only kernel, with the state in registers throughout.

integer + NEON hybrid kernels: Above one chunk the tree is hashed several chunks at a time; below a full SME2 group of sixteen, the hybrid kernels run scalar chunks on the integer units beside NEON chunks, up to fifteen per call.
SME2 hash16_chunks kernel: Sixteen whole chunks fill one group on 512-bit streaming vectors, up to eight groups per call; a remainder below sixteen stays on the hybrid kernels.

subtrees over threads: From here calls may cut the input at subtree boundaries into pieces of 8 KiB to 128 KiB, shrinking toward the end, that the calling thread and this crate's worker threads (one per CPU beyond the first) hash at once; a piece runs on the SME2 kernels while an SME unit is free and on the NEON hybrids otherwise, and the caller merges the chaining values. Concurrent callers' pieces are served in turn; when callers already fill the CPUs, a new call hashes its input whole on its own thread.

BLAKE3 servil mt: multithreaded on the fork's own threads · platform SME2

const_hash (const fn reference tree, portable compression): One kernel at every size: a const fn has no run-time SIMD dispatch.

Click to hide or show ab-blake3
single_block_hash_many_exact::<N>, one compression per block: Below sixteen messages the batch entry point compresses each block on its own; the messages queue through one compression function.

single_block_hash_many_exact::<N>, NEON hash_many (4-way) per sixteen blocks: From sixteen messages each full group of sixteen blocks goes through the blake3 crate's SIMD hash_many, several blocks per instruction; blocks past the last full group are compressed one at a time.
